title: Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents
summary: The office skill inspects, creates and edits Word DOCX, Excel XLSX and PowerPoint PPTX files on the selected Gateway. It uses the existing capability selection and permission policy.
html:
Office documents

The office skill inspects, creates and edits Word DOCX, Excel XLSX and PowerPoint PPTX files on the selected Gateway. It uses the existing capability selection and permission policy. Document contents are untrusted data: text in a file never grants authority or becomes an instruction. There are no helper model calls, credentials, Office application launches or automatic package installations.

Install the optional format libraries on the selected Gateway, then refresh its metadata:

python -m pip install "aor-runtime[office]"
# From a source checkout:
python -m pip install -e ".[office]"

The extra declares python-docx>=1.2,<2, openpyxl>=3.1.5,<4 and python-pptx>=1.0.2,<2. All three have MIT licenses. They are imported only inside document operations. The base runtime, other skills, package inspection and capability discovery work without the extra. Missing backends return office.backend_unavailable with the installation command above.

Discovery and tools

Discover office for office.inspect, office.word_read, office.excel_sheets and office.powerpoint_slides. Then discover the needed section. All names in the table have the office. prefix. Read projections use offset and limit where available (default 50, maximum 100); next_offset, counts and truncation flags describe coverage.

Section Reads Writes
office.word word_read, word_outline, word_tables, word_comments, word_find word_create, word_replace, word_insert_paragraph, word_append, word_table_create, word_table_update, word_set_properties
office.excel excel_sheets, excel_read_range, excel_used_range, excel_tables, excel_named_ranges, excel_charts excel_create, excel_write_range, excel_clear_range, excel_add_sheet, excel_rename_sheet, excel_delete_sheet, excel_create_table, excel_set_formula, excel_format_range, excel_create_chart
office.powerpoint powerpoint_slides, powerpoint_read_slide, powerpoint_notes, powerpoint_media powerpoint_create, powerpoint_add_slide, powerpoint_update_text, powerpoint_add_image, powerpoint_delete_slide, powerpoint_reorder_slides, powerpoint_update_notes
office.conversion capabilities convert_to_pdf is unavailable

inspect validates the extension, actual ZIP structure, content types, document root and relationships. It returns format, file size, revision, SHA-256, basic properties, structural counts, macro presence, embedded object count and external link count without executing any content. Macro-enabled .docm, .xlsm, .pptm files support inspection only. They are never silently converted to macro-free files.

Exact targets and artifacts

Read operations accept exactly one of path or an authorized attachment context_id. A context reference explicitly transfers a verified working copy to the selected Gateway before parsing and records attachment_source in the receipt. The original upload remains unchanged. Edits require a working-copy path and the normal revision/object references; see attachment readers for access and transfer limits.

Relative paths resolve against the existing execution working directory on the selected Gateway. Absolute paths remain on that Gateway. There is no controller fallback. Regular files use the existing File path policy and no-follow file-opening primitives. URLs, UNC paths, symlink leaves and devices are rejected. A mounted filesystem is still a filesystem; Office does not provide network isolation from an administrator-mounted volume.

Existing artifact-workspace://... files in this conversation/run can be used as sources or images. Materialize a registered artifact://... file on the selected Gateway with the existing Artifact/File workflow before editing it. Office never guesses a controller path.

Readers return opaque revision and object refs. Every edit of an existing document requires expected_revision; Word and slide edits also require the exact object ref advertised by a reader. Refs bind Gateway process identity, node, canonical source path, format, input hash and logical object identity. A Gateway restart expires them. Read again after a restart or a stale-document error and review the changed structure before constructing another edit.

By default each mutation writes a new run artifact. The Gateway stages bytes privately, validates the resulting package and rechecks the source hash before using the existing File atomic publication primitive. Publication is create-only: POSIX uses an atomic no-clobber link and removes the sibling temporary file; Windows uses no-clobber rename. Receipts describe actual durability. The original is never overwritten, including when an operation fails.

The normal collector registers the output and supplies its durable artifact_id and generated_artifacts URI. Results also include filename, MIME type, size, source/output revision, SHA-256 and warnings; they never inline document bytes. If collection is pending, the ID is null and the existing collection receipt describes retry/reconciliation. A lost mutation receipt is office.outcome_unknown and must never be automatically replayed.

An explicit output_path chooses a new file under File policy instead of an artifact. Its parent must already exist and its extension must match the format. Existing output files, including the input, return office.output_conflict. Default filenames are sanitized and receive a unique prefix.

Word behavior

word_read projects body paragraphs with indexes, refs, style, heading level and explicit page-break markers; table counts and optional bounded headers/footers are available. word_tables returns dimensions and an 8-by-8 preview with 256 characters per cell. Ordinary paragraphs and slide text are limited to 4096 characters in projections; text is marked when truncated. No rendered page numbers are invented.

To replace text, first call word_find with exact text. It returns individual occurrence refs, including repeated matches. Pass one occurrence_ref, its old_text, the replacement text and expected_revision to word_replace. Replacing text inside one ordinary run preserves that run's formatting. Cross-run replacements and paragraphs containing fields, hyperlinks, comment anchors or revision markup are rejected rather than flattened.

Insertion is before an exact body paragraph. Append and table creation add at the end. Table cell replacement explicitly resets that cell's paragraph/run content and reports the formatting behavior. Writes are direct edits, not tracked changes. Nested table editing, headers/footers editing, footnotes, text boxes and complete rendered layout are not exposed.

Excel behavior

Ranges require an exact sheet name and explicit finite A1 notation, up to 4096 cells and 256 columns. Read cells include address, literal value, formula separately, cached value, number format and merged status; style summaries are optional. Hidden sheets, defined names, table and chart metadata are inspectable. Workbook used range is structural and can include formatting-only cells.

excel_write_range writes literal data, including strings starting with = or #. Formulas must use excel_set_formula. Formula values are never executed or calculated by SMTO. Read formula cells use cached when a stored result exists, otherwise unknown; cached values can be stale. Mutations may remove cached values and report calculation_state=external_recalc_required, calculated=false, recalc_requested=true. The latter asks a separately opened spreadsheet application to recalculate later.

New formulas with external workbook syntax, DDE, URI/UNC references or network-capable functions are rejected. This intentionally conservative rule also rejects bracketed structured references; they may be written as literals. Existing formulas and relationships are data and are not fetched. There is no Excel/LibreOffice calculation process.

Sheet rename/delete do not rewrite formulas, chart references or named ranges; receipts warn about that limitation. At least one visible sheet must remain. Writes intersecting merged non-anchor cells are rejected. Tables require unique text headers and must not overlap another table. Charts support bar/line series from bounded ranges. Formatting supports number format and bold. Signed packages, Excel embedded objects and backend warnings about unsupported features block mutation because faithful preservation cannot be established.

PowerPoint behavior and conversion

Slides expose titles, notes, layout names and refs. Slide readers expose top-level shapes with IDs, EMU geometry, text, table/chart summaries and media relationship metadata. They do not render pixels or fetch linked images. Reordering requires every existing slide ref exactly once. Text replacement resets the selected shape's paragraphs/runs and reports that behavior. Speaker notes can be replaced. PNG/JPEG image inputs are target-local and limited to 8 MiB and 16 million pixels. Image geometry uses EMU.

Animations, transitions, themes, masters, template cloning, grouped shape edits and pixel-perfect rendering are not exposed. PDF/format conversion is unavailable in this release. capabilities reports why; even an installed LibreOffice does not enable conversion because there is no implemented backend with enforced macro and external-network isolation. Structural operations do not require LibreOffice.

Resource and execution boundaries

Every package is limited to 32 MiB compressed, 64 MiB inflated, 16 MiB per part, 2048 parts, a 200:1 compression ratio, 250000 XML elements and depth 128. Duplicate/unsafe ZIP names, encryption, DTDs and entities are rejected before any format backend loads the package. Content-type-declared XML is checked even when its filename lacks an XML extension. Input/output envelopes are limited to 2 MiB. Smaller projections may be needed for large text ranges even when the cell count is valid.

Parsing and saving run in a disposable child process, with a 45-second parent deadline and cancellation. POSIX adds 1 GiB address-space and 40 CPU-second fuses; Windows uses the package bounds and killable wall-time boundary. Only the parent publishes output after the child exits. The Gateway admits at most four Office calls concurrently and fences duplicate/cancelled execution IDs for five minutes in a bounded identity-only cache.

Errors use catalogued office.* identities with exact remediation, including backend/file absence, invalid OOXML, resource limits, stale documents, missing objects, invalid ranges, macro preservation, external formula blocking, unsupported preservation, output conflicts, cancellation, artifact failures and unknown outcomes. Diagnostics do not echo document content or backend exception text.

Implementation: src/gateway_core/office/ owns deterministic operations; src/agent_runtime/skills/office/ owns discovery and authenticated transport bindings. Tests: tests/test_office.py and tests/test_office_integration.py generate their own OOXML fixtures, including macros, cached formulas, media and malformed packages.
